chunks: Ya‘qūb ibn Shu‘ayb asked Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام.
About a man who lends another man inferior dirhams, then takes from him fresh, better dirhams, while he is content with that.
So he said: There is no harm in it. And that was mentioned from ‘Alī عليه السلام.

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمَ: dirhams, the monetary units involved in the transaction
key_terms.طَيِّبَةً بِهَا نَفْسُهُ: being pleased and content with it
key_terms.عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam ‘Alī عليه السلام, from whom the same ruling is reported
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to repay a loan of lower-quality dirhams with better-quality dirhams in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a loan involving dirhams of differing quality. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm in receiving better dirhams in repayment when the exchange is agreeable, and the same ruling is also reported from Imam ‘Alī عليه السلام.
